latin.605: GAR. Resp. I. Qui negant nos in ipsa Adami persona fuisse morti addictos, illi manifeste deserunt Confessionem Ecclesiarum nostrarum, quae id docet & dicit expresse Art. 10.
latin.606: PLAC. Egone illam Confessionem desero, quam totam amplector, arcteque teneo, imprimis articulum illum decimum? At nego nos in ipsa Adami persona fuisse morti addictos. Primum illa verba, fuisse morti addictos, mea non sunt: neque praeterito usus sum, sed praesenti, neque de addictione locutus sum, sed de ipsa morte. Verba enim Apostoli sic aiunt: in Adam omnes moriuntur, ita & in Christo omnes vivificabuntur; de praesenti eiusmodi addictione intelligi non possunt, ut ex futuro, vivificabuntur, perspicuum est.
latin.607: Loquor igitur de morte qua quisque moritur, de resurrectione qua quisque formaliter resurgit. Nec aliud volo, cum nego nos mori in ipsa Adami persona, quam nos mori ipsa morte Adami nobis imputata; cum nego nos resurgere in ipsa Christi persona, quam resurgere resurrectione Christi nobis imputata, ut patet ex verbis ipsis antecedentibus.
latin.608: Contrariumne docet Art. ille Confessionis decimus? Cur igitur cum illo committo? At dicit nos in ipsius (Adami) persona spoliatos bonis illis omnibus, in omnem hanc miseriam & maledictionem incidisse. Ergo morimur in ipsa Adami persona, hoc est morte Adami nobis imputata. Nihil tale sequitur ex illis Confessionis verbis. Imo ne imputatio quidem ulla ex ijs colligi potest, vel donorum illorum, vel spoliationis illius, ut plenius declarabitur cap. XII.
latin.609: GAR. 2. Unionem cum Adamo naturalem non tantum agnoscimus, sed etiam imputationis illius, de qua agitur, fundamentum esse dicimus.
latin.610: PLAC. Si imputatio intelligitur antecedens seu immediata, non est illius fundamentum unio illa. Sed pergat.

pass_a.605: Garrigues's first reply: anyone who denies we were devoted to death in Adam's person has deserted the churches' Confession, which Art. 10 states expressly.
pass_a.606: Placeus refuses the desertion charge—he holds the whole Confession, especially Art. 10—yet still denies 'were devoted to death in Adam's person.' He rejects Garrigues's wording: Placeus spoke present death, not past addiction; Paul's 'die / will be made alive' is not about a present devotion of that kind.
pass_a.607: He clarifies the denial: each dies and rises his own formal death/rising. Denying we die in Adam's person means denying we die by Adam's death imputed; denying we rise in Christ's person means denying we rise by Christ's resurrection imputed—read from the prior words.
pass_a.608: Placeus asks whether Art. 10 really teaches the contrary. From 'spoiled of goods in Adam's person and fallen into misery' Garrigues infers dying by Adam's death imputed. Placeus denies the leap: those Confession words yield neither that conclusion nor any imputation of the gifts or the spoiling—fuller in Cap. XII.
pass_a.609: GAR opens a second head: natural union with Adam is not only granted but called the foundation of the imputation in dispute.
pass_a.610: Tip: Placeus grants natural union, but if the imputation meant is antecedent or immediate, that union is not its foundation—and he invites Garrigues to continue. Tip before the mortem Adami imputari exchange.

605: GAR. Resp. I. Those who deny that we were devoted to death in Adam's own person plainly desert the Confession of our churches, which teaches and expressly says that in Art. 10.
606: PLAC. Do I desert that Confession, which I wholly embrace and tightly hold, especially that tenth article? Yet I deny that we were devoted to death in Adam's own person. First, those words "were devoted to death" are not mine: I did not use the past tense but the present, and I did not speak of devotion (addiction) but of death itself. For the Apostle's words run thus: in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive; they cannot be taken of a present devotion of that kind, as is clear from the future "will be made alive."
607: I speak, then, of the death by which each dies, and of the resurrection by which each formally rises. And when I deny that we die in Adam's own person, I mean nothing else than that we die by Adam's own death imputed to us; when I deny that we rise in Christ's own person, nothing else than that we rise by Christ's resurrection imputed to us—as is plain from the very words that went before.
608: Does that tenth article of the Confession teach the contrary? Why then am I set against it? But it says we were spoiled of all those goods in his (Adam's) person, and fell into all this misery and curse. Therefore we die in Adam's own person—that is, by Adam's death imputed to us. No such thing follows from those words of the Confession. Indeed not even any imputation can be drawn from them, either of those gifts or of that spoiling—as will be shown more fully in chapter XII.
609: GAR. 2. We not only acknowledge a natural union with Adam, but also say that it is the foundation of that imputation which is under discussion.
610: PLAC. If the imputation is understood as antecedent or immediate, that union is not its foundation. But let him go on.
